children: Talisker Resources Ltd. will remove the laser sorter from Bralorne’s plant, opting for XRT-only sorting that rejected 57–67% waste with ~84–87% gold recovery, and expects to cut about $4M in capex while simplifying operations for its DSO phase.
Immediate capital reduction and simpler plant lowers funding needs and execution risk.
Maintains strong gold capture while enabling waste rejection central to DSO economics.
Cuts mass to ship/process, reducing opex in crushing, trucking, and processing.
Avoids grade dilution and higher shipping mass that would hurt margins.
Improved grade control could lift realized head grades and cash flow per tonne.

This is an operational optimization in Talisker’s DSO phase, aligning with prior efforts to enhance grade and reduce shipped mass. Next, investors will look for updated cost/throughput guidance, realized DSO margins, and timelines that validate these test gains in production.
Based on the original press release from Talisker Resources Ltd. distributed by GlobeNewswire.
